name: Qwen Image 2.1 - with the community "Fix" LoRA
description:
The same Qwen Image 2.1 text-to-image model as the plain bundle, plus a community adapter that aims to clean up its weak spots - and, just as importantly, the sampling settings its author ships with it.

Built to be compared. Run the plain "Qwen Image 2.1" bundle and this one with the SAME prompt and the SAME seed and look at the two side by side. Easier still: set "Fix strength" to 0 here, which keeps every other setting identical and shows you the same seed without the adapter.

Two things differ from the plain bundle, and it is worth knowing which is which. The adapter itself changes composition noticeably - it tends toward a glossier, shallower-focus photograph. The settings (guidance raised from 1 to 3, a different sampler, and two model patches) are what sharpen detail and fix muddled small print like a watch dial. On the pictures tested here a good part of the improvement came from the settings rather than the adapter, which is exactly what "Fix strength 0" lets you check for yourself.

Guidance above 1 is also why this bundle has a negative prompt at all. At the plain bundle's guidance of 1 a negative prompt does nothing, which is why it does not offer one.

It is MUCH slower: about 46 s against the plain bundle's 14 s on this machine, a bit over 3x. That is arithmetic, not a fault - guidance above 1 makes the model run twice per step, and the seeds_2 sampler is a second-order solver that runs it twice again. Same VRAM (about 15 GB), since the adapter merges into the computation rather than sitting in memory.
